purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered Dublin City NIAH buildings on Talbot Street

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: Official national CSV location fields include ITM and latitude/longitude. Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are retained as raw page values because the pages do not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: Living Island
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010200 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house, built c.1840, now in commercial use. Pitched slate roof with shared brown-brick chimneystacks and terracotta pots to west stack behind rendered parapet with painted masonry coping. Rendered walls with channelled render quoins; square-headed windows with masonry sills and single-pane timber sliding sashes; cast-iron balconettes to first-floor windows. Recent timber shopfront with panelled engaged pilasters and shaped consoles/fascia. NIAH appraisal identifies retained timber sashes and balconettes as notable features and notes the building's contribution to the 1840s Talbot Street terrace.

candidate_records.name: Continental Foods Cash and Carry
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010201 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house with dormer attic, built c.1840, now commercial. Pitched slate roof, shared brown-brick stacks, terracotta pots, front dormer windows, brown-brick parapet, Flemish-bond upper walling, gauged square-headed openings, timber sliding sashes and recent shopfront. The NIAH appraisal notes surviving timber sashes and the building's coherent form within the north-side Talbot Street terrace laid out following the sale of Tyrone House.

candidate_records.name: Gerry Keane Paints/Wallpaper
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010202 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house with dormer attic, built c.1840, now commercial. Pitched slate roof with shared red-brick stacks and gable-fronted dormer behind brown-brick parapet; Flemish-bond brickwork over red-brick platband; gauged square-headed windows, replacement uPVC windows and steel balconettes; recent shared timber shopfront with bolection mouldings and polished granite plinths. NIAH appraisal notes the building maintains the terrace's fenestration rhythm and parapet height.

candidate_records.name: Aroma Foods
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010204 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.source_discrepancy: National CSV IN_USE_AS_TYPE is blank. Individual NIAH page lists Historical Use as shop/retail outlet and describes the building as currently vacant. Preserve these as separate source fields; do not infer a current commercial tenant or use.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced two-bay three-storey house, built c.1840, with recent timber shopfront. Flat roof with shared red-brick stacks behind brown-brick parapet; Flemish-bond brickwork; gauged square-headed windows with masonry sills and single-pane timber sliding sashes; timber shopfront and separate panelled door with overlight to upper floors. NIAH appraisal says its modest scale maintains the street's fenestration rhythm and parapet line.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number searches against open repository issues and pull requests.
duplicate_screen.result: No open issue or pull request matches returned for any of the five exact registration numbers at time of research.

identity_and_spatial_cautions: Nos.12-16 Talbot Street are five separately registered terrace houses. Preserve each registration separately even where neighbouring descriptions mention shared chimney stacks, rainwater goods or shopfronts.

Nos.13 and 14 share the commercial name Gerry Keane Paints/Wallpaper in the NIAH register but are separate registered buildings with different façades and descriptions. Do not collapse them into one business/place record without separate building entities and an explicit shared-use relationship.

No.12 (50010204) has a blank IN_USE_AS_TYPE in the national CSV. The individual page lists Historical Use as shop/retail outlet and says currently vacant. Retain this source distinction; do not state the building is currently occupied by Aroma Foods.
All five page coordinate pairs are raw unlabelled values. The official CSV ITM and latitude/longitude fields are stored independently; never substitute page coordinates for CSV values.
Shared chimney stacks and continuous terrace rhythm are relationships/components, not additional archive objects without independent object-level evidence.
NIAH use and condition descriptions are survey-time source statements. No present-day condition, occupancy, public access or ownership has been verified.
explicitly_not_done: No source registry or visual inventory imports
No map pins or coordinate imports
